overview: This 192-page file traces Japanese merchant shipping from the losses of 1931 to expansion and wartime controls in 1938. Consular reports, statistics, translated legislation, and correspondence document fleet growth, route competition, shipbuilding, cargo preferences, and shipping in China. A substantial exchange concerns an alleged plot to bomb the Hiyu Maru in Seattle and requests to protect Japanese vessels in American ports.
interest: Translated shipping laws, detailed fleet surveys, and cargo-routing inquiries reveal how commercial shipping became a matter of state policy.
